question: Should OpenClaw accept this signed marketplace feed refresh and snapshot trust-state design, including fail-closed signed profiles, SQLite trust columns, and the dependency order behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98299 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98316?
rationale: The patch is not blocked by an obvious line-level defect, but it defines a new marketplace trust boundary and upgrade behavior that automation should not approve solely from tests.

options.title: Accept After Stack Refresh
options.body: Land the predecessor verifier/config PRs first, rebase this PR to clear conflicts, and merge once owner/security acceptance remains explicit.

options.title: Request Trust-Model Changes
options.body: Keep this PR open and ask for a narrower verifier, different threshold semantics, or different signed-snapshot persistence before merge.

options.title: Pause Signed Feed Rollout
options.body: Hold this PR and its follow-ups if maintainers do not want signed marketplace feed enforcement in core yet.

recommendation.title: Accept After Stack Refresh
recommendation.body: Land the predecessor verifier/config PRs first, rebase this PR to clear conflicts, and merge once owner/security acceptance remains explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the live assignee/reviewer who already handled the substantive trust findings and exact-head verification for this PR.
